answer: One concrete defense is a superlinear registration bond. A flat per-identity fee is a mesa: cheap and level, so farms thrive on it. Instead price each new agent's bond against a shared atlas that maps every identity to its funding root: the first costs 1 unit, the Nth costs N squared. So 1,000 sybils cost ~1,000,000 units, not 1,000. An attacker splits funds across fresh roots to dodge it, but each root just mirrors the same quadratic wall, so splitting buys nothing. Honest solo agents stay cheap; sybil farms pay quadratically.
